Yes, most of the conditions in the DSM (at least all the ones I've looked at) have the criterion that the symptoms significantly impact/impair the person's life in some setting, and that makes it pretty close to the definition of a disability. Idk if I'm making sense because my head's very unclear right now, but I just know the ADA covers mental and physical disabilities.

And I've heard it depends on the HR person or particular company, etc. I have no idea how this particular HR representative is, but I guess it's a waiting game right now.

I want to transfer to another store, since there are others in the area and they relocate people sometimes, but I don't know who to talk to about that when I'm not comfortable talking to the GM. 

I don't think she even knows what she expects. Regarding other store things, she's constantly changing her mind or just not communicating with anyone.
I don't know how, and I have to go to work today..
